summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with symptoms of a urinary tract infection, left lower quadrant pain, headache, dizziness, and hallucinations. She had recently been discharged after a kidney transplant and was found to have a supratherapeutic tacrolimus level of 23, which was adjusted to 3mg twice daily, leading to clinical improvement. She was diagnosed with an E. coli UTI resistant to ampicillin and ciprofloxacin, treated initially with ceftriaxone and later transitioned to oral cefpodoxime. Abdominal cellulitis near her JP drain site was treated with doxycycline, with visible improvement. Her ureteral stent was removed on hospital day 2, and the JP drain was discontinued prior to discharge. She was discharged home in good condition with instructions to continue antibiotics, adjust anticoagulation with warfarin, and await further tacrolimus dosing guidance from the transplant team.
